scope: Second independent read-only CPU review. No source, service, GPU, HTTP, JIT, NVCC, or compilation action was performed.

evidence: prefill.py creates the carrier at admission and passes the same PendingReq carrier to continuations.
cache.py snapshots into the carrier; attention/linear.py consults the carrier before ordinary ping-pong tracking.
cache.py implements singleton _D09BoundaryEntry, exact logical match length, lock count, cache-size accounting, rebuild reset, and allocation-pressure eviction.
The sealed 20282 and 22558 page_size=64 cold-commit tests verify exact logical matching, whole physical-page retention, state restoration, and idle integrity.
limitations: The new tests do not admit a second request from an existing exact entry and advance/forward its tail.
They do not validate copy-on-write or mapping ownership of the remainder of a partially shared physical page.

findings.trigger: A new request matches an existing non-page-aligned D09 entry at boundary 20282 or 22558 and has a nonempty tail.
source_evidence: cache.py:139 constructs _D09BoundaryHandle with cached_len equal to the exact boundary.
cache.py:20-24 makes get_matched_indices expose only indices[:cached_len].
prefill.py:139-141 copies only those logical boundary indices into the new request page table.
cache.py:418-433 allocates from ceil(cached_len/page_size), so it does not allocate or write page-table positions [boundary, ceil(boundary/64)*64).

concrete_geometry.boundary_20282: 20282 mod 64 = 58; page-table positions 20282..20287 are not copied or allocated.
concrete_geometry.boundary_22558: 22558 mod 64 = 62; page-table positions 22558..22559 are not copied or allocated.

findings.impact: The first tail forward uses unmapped default/stale physical-page locations for those residual tokens. This is a KV ownership and aliasing defect: the exact entry claims full-page ownership but a hit neither transfers/COWs the partial page nor supplies valid mappings for the tail. It can corrupt the sentinel or unrelated KV storage and cannot be accepted without a targeted CPU mapping/COW test and repair.
required_repair_proof: Admit a second request from an exact 20282 and 22558 entry, then assert every page-table position through ceil(boundary/64) is valid and ownership-safe before the tail forward.
Exercise a tail write or equivalent page-table mapping simulation and prove the original entry remains valid for a concurrent/next exact hit, or prove an explicit COW transfer policy.
Run integrity, lock/refcount, eviction, and rebuild assertions after the hit-tail-finish lifecycle.

cpu_tests.base_comparison: The same three failures predate D09. Each expects a 3-tuple but the base's established PromptAdmitted contract produces (uid, prompt_tokens, cached_tokens, epoch). They remain recorded and are not used as a D09 regression verdict.

stop_condition: Second independent CPU review complete. The overlap carrier repair is supported by CPU evidence, but exact-entry hit-tail page mapping/COW has a P0 blocker.
